newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Islamist group says rights abuses rise.
newsitem.headline: Turk Islamist group says rights abuses rise.

text.p: An Islamist human rights group said on Tuesday that violations of religious rights had risen in Turkey in July.

"Human rights violations rose in July and keep rising every month. The picture of rights abuses in Turkey is unfortunately very dark," Ahmet Mercan, head of the Istanbul branch of the Mazlumder group, told Reuters.
The report focused on rights abuses in connection with religious freedom.
It said 15 people were fired from their jobs for religious reasons, 37 women were targeted under a ban on Islamic headscarves and one Koran teaching centre was shut down in July.

Civil servants are banned from wearing Islamic headgear to work under strict laws dating from the 1920s. The laws were introduced by the founder of the officially secular Turkish republic, Mustafa Kemal Ataturk.
Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, Necmettin Erbakan, resigned in June amid demands from the military to crack down on what the army saw as rising Islamic activism.
A central demand is a secularist plan to limit religious schooling, which has drawn angry protests from Islamists.
Erbakan was replaced at the end of June by a secularist government under Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz who promised to put the army's demands into practice.

The report said there were a total of 786 cases of human rights abuses in July in Turkey. It said 395 people were detained, 96 died in clashes, 14 said they had been tortured and seven died in prison riots.
Turkey has often been criticised for its poor human rights record, which has damaged relations with its Western partners.
"Turkey willingly excludes itself from the world, because of its human rights situation and it escalates the process of the its alienation," Mercan said.
